title: Learning to Schedule in Diffusion Probabilistic Models

problem.claim: Hand-crafted sampling schedules in DDIM rely on human expertise and may not account for all relevant factors in the sampling process; a shared schedule may also be invalid for all instances.

gap.claim: Existing DDIM scheduling does not automatically adapt sampling schedules to the current noisy image or to differences among instances.

contributions.claim: A reinforcement-learning method automatically searches for a sampling schedule for diffusion probabilistic models.
A policy network predicts the next sampling step from the current state of the noisy image.
The policy network is optimized with an episodic actor-critic reinforcement-learning framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Empirical results are reported to show superiority over various datasets with different timesteps.
The trained sampling schedule is reported to generalize strongly across different diffusion probabilistic model baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion probabilistic models have advanced generative modeling.
DDIM reduces inference computation by skipping steps.
DDIM's hand-crafted and shared sampling schedule has limitations.
The paper uses reinforcement learning and a policy network to search for adaptive sampling schedules.
The authors report superiority across datasets and timesteps and strong generalization across diffusion model baselines.
